title: PreMarket Prep Recap For May 1: Feuerstein Breaks Down Neurotrope's Data Spin; Contrarian Vs. Momentum Investing
summary: This article recaps the May 1st PreMarket Prep show, featuring an analysis by Adam Feuerstein on Neurotrope Inc.'s Alzheimer's drug data, which he characterized as a "spin" on a failed study. The show also covered key technical levels for stocks like Twitter, Tribune Media, Amazon, Foot Locker, and Workday, along with a discussion on the merits of contrarian versus momentum investing in the current market climate.

title: Angie's List to be acquired by HomeAdvisor parent company IAC
summary: Angie's List has agreed to be acquired by IAC, the parent company of rival HomeAdvisor, for over $500 million. The deal, expected to close in the fourth quarter, will form a new publicly traded company called ANGI Homeservices Inc., headquartered in Golden, Colo., and led by HomeAdvisor CEO Chris Terrill. This acquisition marks a significant shift for Angie's List, which had previously rejected an offer from IAC and struggled with its subscription-based business model in recent years.

title: Exclusive - Blackstone's GSO snaps up J. Crew debt in restructuring gambit
summary: GSO Capital Partners, Blackstone's credit arm, is acquiring J. Crew Group Inc.'s debt in a strategic move that could help the struggling retailer avoid bankruptcy and provide a profitable outcome for GSO. J. Crew faces significant debt, including $567 million in unsecured bonds due in 2019, and is attempting a restructuring by placing its brand's intellectual property into a new company. GSO aims to gain a controlling position in J. Crew's loan to facilitate this restructuring, despite resistance from other creditors who view the intellectual property carve-out as a default risk.

title: MAC Is Having A Mysterious Flash Sale At Ulta Today
summary: MAC is holding a mysterious flash sale at Ulta today, offering 50% off a "can't live without" product for a limited time. This event precedes MAC's official launch on Ulta.com on May 7th and in select stores in June, marking a significant expansion of MAC's retail presence beyond department stores and its own boutiques. The partnership will bring MAC products and in-house makeup services to over 100 Ulta locations in 2017.

title: Angie’s List will merge with HomeAdvisor after finally accepting IAC’s acquisition offer
summary: Angie's List has finally agreed to merge with IAC's HomeAdvisor, forming a new public company called ANGI Homeservices. The deal values Angie's List at $8.50 per share, or approximately $500 million, representing a 44.3 percent premium over its Monday closing price. This merger aims to combine the strengths of both companies to become a dominant force in the home services marketplace, transitioning towards an on-demand model.

title: F5 Networks will move HQ to glitzy new Seattle skyscraper, to be called ‘F5 Tower’
summary: F5 Networks has leased all the office space in a new Seattle skyscraper previously known as The Mark, which will now be named F5 Tower. The company will move all its Seattle employees to the new headquarters in 2019, occupying 516,000 square feet of office space. The lease term is 14.5 years, costing F5 Networks $359.5 million.

title: Tech company F5 will lease all of downtown’s newest office tower
summary: F5 Networks, a Seattle technology company, will lease all 28 floors of a new office tower under construction on Fifth and Columbia in downtown Seattle, which will be named F5 Tower. The company is moving from its waterfront complex to accommodate growth and will have space for its 1,375 Seattle employees with room to expand. The 14.5-year lease is valued at $359.5 million, reflecting the strong demand for office space in downtown Seattle.

title: Target will step up Amazon Prime competition with household-essentials delivery
summary: Target Corp. is launching a new service called "Target Restock" to compete with Amazon.com's Pantry service by offering household-essentials delivery. The service aims to replace the traditional "Target Run" for stocking up on supplies. It is unclear if Hawaii, with its six Target stores, will be included in the initial rollout.

title: Weis Markets brings online shopping, grocery pickup service to State College
summary: Weis Markets has launched an online shopping and curbside pickup service at its State College (Martin Street) location, allowing customers to order groceries online and pick them up at the store. The service, which carries a fee waived for first-time orders or orders over $150, mirrors a growing trend among major retailers like Amazon and Walmart. Weis's online service is already available in 37 locations across multiple states.

title: Apple Investing $200 Million In American Facility For Scratch-Resistant Glass
summary: Apple announced an investment of $200 million in Corning Inc.'s Harrodsburg, Kentucky facility, dedicated to producing scratch-resistant Gorilla Glass for its iPhones and iPads. This investment is the first from Apple's $1 billion Advanced Manufacturing Fund, aimed at supporting U.S.-based companies, and acknowledges Corning's crucial role in developing the glass that replaced plastic screens on early iPhones. The partnership has created 1,000 U.S. jobs, and this funding will sustain the 400 employees in Harrodsburg, adding to Kentucky's recent significant business investments.

title: If You Invested in Amazon at Its IPO, You Would Be a Millionaire Today
summary: This article highlights the hypothetical massive returns an early investment in Amazon's IPO would have yielded, illustrating that a $5,000 investment 20 years ago would now be worth $2.4 million. It explores how this reflects on investors like Warren Buffett, who regretted not buying Amazon early, and details the company's tumultuous stock performance, including its dot-com bubble rise and subsequent dip, before its massive growth to a $457.9 billion market cap.

title: Domino’s stock is up about 5,000 percent since 2008
summary: Domino's Pizza Inc. experienced a remarkable resurgence after hitting a low of $3.85 a share in 2008, with its stock price soaring by about 5,000 percent. This turnaround was driven by a complete overhaul of its pizza recipe, rooting out poor franchisees, and aggressively embracing digital technology for ordering. The company has seen 24 consecutive quarters of U.S. same-store sales growth, expanded globally to 14,000 stores, and now processes over 60 percent of its orders digitally, referring to itself as a "technology company."

title: Wal-Mart experiments with tech-enhanced ‘Next-Gen’ stores
summary: Wal-Mart is testing new "Next-Gen" supercenter layouts in Tomball, TX, and Lake Nona, FL, integrating technology and revised merchandising to enhance the shopping experience. These stores feature improved "Scan and Go" checkout, interactive displays for connected devices and an "endless aisle" for online items, and Wi-Fi buttons to page staff. This initiative is part of a broader effort by Wal-Mart and other traditional retailers like Target to blend e-commerce and brick-and-mortar experiences, as research indicates physical stores can boost online sales and serve as crucial fulfillment hubs.

title: Students Partner With Boeing to Strengthen Computer Security
summary: Cal State Fullerton computer science students partnered with the Boeing Co. to develop new computer security approaches. This collaboration, initiated by Boeing through CSUF's Center for Cybersecurity, focused on creating methodologies to measure the effectiveness of security controls against cyberattacks. The project provided students with valuable industry experience and insights into safeguarding critical systems for large corporations.

summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares (VCR) holdings. It lists the top 10 companies, their percentage of total assets, and sector weightings. The ETF aims to track the performance of an index composed of U.S. consumer discretionary companies.

title: Chinese Online Retailer Developing One-ton Delivery Drones
summary: Chinese online retailer JD.com Inc. is developing one-ton delivery drones and plans to test them in Shaanxi province to transport consumer goods to remote areas and farm produce to cities. This initiative is part of the industry's effort to expand into rural areas and overcome delivery cost challenges, with the company aiming for a network capable of inter-city and inter-province logistics. JD.com also reported a significant increase in first-quarter revenue and a return to profit.

title: Thousands of protesters brand McDonald's the 'Trump of corporations'
summary: Thousands of protesters in Chicago branded McDonald's the "Trump of corporations" during a demonstration ahead of the company's annual shareholder meeting. Organized by groups like Fight for $15, the protestors cited low wages, sexual harassment, and the company's alleged avoidance of taxes, drawing parallels to Donald Trump's business practices. The protests aimed to raise the minimum wage and advocate for workers' rights to unionize.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch Posts First Quarter Loss of $62 Million
summary: Abercrombie & Fitch reported a smaller-than-expected first-quarter loss of $62 million, with comparable-store sales declining 3 percent but beating analyst expectations. The company, which is up for sale, saw strong demand for its Hollister brand, which helped offset overall declines. Rival American Eagle Outfitters and private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management are reportedly planning a joint bid.

title: Report: Wal-Mart remodeling hundreds of stores to ease in-store pickup
summary: Walmart is investing millions to remodel between 400 and 640 physical stores to improve the in-store pickup experience and overall customer shopping journey. Changes include widening aisles, improving sight-lines, moving pickup services to the front, and expanding fresh food sections. This initiative reflects a broader trend among traditional retailers like Target to invest in brick-and-mortar stores to enhance omnichannel sales and compete with e-commerce.

title: A new rival for Elon Musk has just blasted off in the space race
summary: Rocket Lab, a Silicon Valley-funded space company, successfully launched a battery-powered, 3-D printed rocket into space from New Zealand, marking a new competitor in the race for cheap space access. This successful test is the first of three trial flights before planned commercial take-offs later in the year, distinguishing itself by focusing on cheap, disposable rockets rather than reusable ones like those pursued by Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. Rocket Lab aims for over 50 launches annually, positioning New Zealand as a significant player in the global satellite launch industry.

title: Target Is Said to Invest $75 Million in Bedding Startup Casper
summary: Target Corp. is reportedly investing $75 million in the online mattress seller Casper Sleep Inc. This investment is part of Target's strategy to enhance its e-commerce presence amidst declining brick-and-mortar sales. The deal follows Target's earlier consideration of acquiring the entire Casper business.

title: Amazon.com Inc shares hit US$1,000 for first time, showing its dominance in e-commerce and cloud tech
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares surpassed US$1,000 for the first time, highlighting its dominant positions in e-commerce and cloud computing. The company's US$478 billion market value is double that of Walmart, driven by investors' confidence in its global growth potential and its Amazon Web Services (AWS) division. Analysts predict further growth due to Amazon's strong performance in massive global industries.

title: Analysts grill Ugg owner for ‘dangerous’ Macy’s expansion
summary: Deckers Outdoor Corp., owner of Ugg, Teva, and Deckers brands, is expanding Ugg concessions to 200 Macy's stores while ending contracts with smaller accounts, a move that Wall Street analysts deem "dangerous" due to Macy's discounting practices. This strategy contradicts Ugg's goal of improving average selling prices and controlling inventory. Analysts point to Coach's successful strategy of pulling back from department stores to protect margins as a cautionary tale for Ugg.
